narrative:
The 2020 Toronto Blue Jays were a team finding their footing in one of baseball's strangest seasons — a 60-game sprint played without fans, with Toronto unable to even use their own stadium, bouncing between Buffalo and a borrowed home in Dunedin. They stumbled out of the gate in July, going 3-4 while their bullpen and back-end starters absorbed brutal damage. Kiermaier's triple in the opener set an ominous tone, and the early weeks made it look like a long summer was ahead.

August told a more complicated story. The relief corps continued to leak runs — Font, Hatch, Romano, Shoemaker, and Cole all surrendered pivotal home runs against Atlanta and Tampa — yet the Blue Jays went 15-12 that month, their best stretch of the season. The difference was the offense. Rowdy Tellez delivered clutch two-RBI singles, Randal Grichuk emerged as an unlikely hero with walk-off and go-ahead shots, and Teoscar Hernández proved he could change a game in a single at-bat. The biggest play of the season came on August 28th, when Grichuk launched a two-run blast worth nearly 0.85 WPA to rescue a game Toronto desperately needed.

September was a grind. The Blue Jays went 14-13, surviving on grit and just enough timely hitting. Hernández's three-run homer on September 3rd was a bright spot, but the bullpen remained a liability — Anthony Bass and Rafael Dolis surrendered gut-punch moments against Baltimore and Philadelphia. Still, the Jays did what they needed to do, clawing into the expanded postseason field and earning a Wild Card matchup against the Tampa Bay Rays.

The postseason was brief and painful. Over two games against Tampa, the Blue Jays ran into the buzzsaw that was Randy Arozarena and a Rays lineup that simply wouldn't stop scoring. Robbie Ray couldn't hold leads, Hyun Jin Ryu was hammered in Game 2 — surrendering a Zunino two-run shot and then a Hunter Renfroe grand slam that turned a close game into a blowout. The offense managed moments — a Biggio double, some baserunners — but could never sustain a rally. A promising young team's season ended abruptly in the Wild Card round, leaving the promise of what's next as the dominant feeling heading into the offseason.

chapters.title: A Rocky Launch
chapters.description: Toronto's pitching staff absorbs crushing early blows as the team stumbles to a 3-4 July record.

chapters.title: Grichuk Rises, Bullpen Burns
chapters.description: Randal Grichuk and Teoscar Hernández ignite the offense even as the relief corps keeps giving games away.

chapters.title: Clutch Hits Save August
chapters.description: Rowdy Tellez, Grichuk's walk-off homer, and Hernández's game-winning single carry Toronto to a winning August record.

chapters.title: Grinding Into October
chapters.description: The Blue Jays survive a .519 September on the strength of Hernández's bat while the bullpen continues to wobble.

chapters.title: Wild Card Heartbreak
chapters.description: Tampa Bay's potent lineup overwhelms Toronto's pitching across two Wild Card games, ending the Jays' postseason run.
